authored.summary: A moving average that speeds up when price trends cleanly and nearly stops when it chops sideways
authored.description:
## What it shows
A line on the price chart that follows **Source** (the close by default) at a speed set by the market itself. Over the last **Length** bars (14 by default) it measures the efficiency ratio: how far price got, divided by the total distance it travelled bar by bar. A ratio of 1 is a perfectly clean trend and 0 is pure back-and-forth. The line then moves toward price at a rate between a **Fast length** average (2 by default) and a **Slow length** average (30 by default), squared, so choppy stretches barely move it. It is green while rising and red while falling, and the efficiency ratio appears in the Data Window.

## How to read it
- A flat line means price is going nowhere efficiently; many traders stand aside until it tilts.
- A line that turns and steepens shows a trend with follow-through; its colour flips on the turn.
- Price holding on one side of the line in a trend is a common trailing reference.
- Alerts are available for **KAMA turned up** and **KAMA turned down**.

## Limits
- It adapts to efficiency, not direction, so a sharp reversal still takes a few bars to show.
- In a slow grind with many small pullbacks it can stay flatter than a plain moving average.
- Nothing is drawn until **Length** bars are loaded; the first value is that bar's close.
